Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Economy Average lending rate fell marginally to 15.75% in October 2026 Source : Joy Business 18 November 2026 11:39am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The average lending rate fell marginally from 15.94% in August 2026 to 15.74% in October 2026.
This means one would pay about 1.31% per month on every loan, excluding other fees.
According to data from the Bank of Ghana, the average cost of borrowing has remained within the 15% bracket since May 2026.
Similarly, the Ghana Reference Rate stood at 10.01 in October 2026, a reduction from 10.61% in August 2026.
According to the Bank of Ghana’s November 2026 Summary of Economic and Financial Data, the average lending rate stood at 20.58% in January 2026, but fell to 19.17% in February 2026 and subsequently to 17.74% in March 2026.
It hovered around 15.83%, 15.64%, 15.80% and 15.78% in May 2026, June 2026, July 2026 and August 2026, respectively.
In September 2026, the Bank of Ghana held its policy rate unchanged at 14%, citing risks to inflation and external pressure emanating from the Middle East war that had pushed oil prices very high.
The average lending rates, however, vary among banks, the sectors they lend to, and borrowers.
Some banks offer loans equivalent to the Ghana Reference Rate, whilst others will charge rates as high as 30% per annum.
Presently, some banks are offering structured loans to employees at about 12% on the average.
